source.ref: Maharashtra Stamp Act, 1958, Sch. I Art. 40(a)
source.quoted_text: Sch I Art. 40(a) (both columns): 'when possession of the property or any part of the property comprised in such deed is given by the mortgagor or agreed to be given — The same duty as is leviable on a conveyance under clauses (a), (b) or (c), as the case may be, of Article 25, for the amount secured by such deed.' Explanation I: a mortgagor giving the mortgagee a POA to collect rents or a lease is deemed to give possession.

pending_verification.reason: The transport surcharge reaches usufructuary mortgages in notified cities, but this rule has no sourced subtype/city modifier. Restrict computation to a positively identified non-usufructuary mortgage outside the metro-cess area.

source.ref: Maharashtra Act III of 2021, ss.1(2), 3(b), pp.1-2
source.quoted_text: Section 1(2) deems the Act in force on 9 February 2021. Section 3(b) substitutes Article 40(b): (i) up to Rs 5 lakh, 0.1% subject to a Rs 100 minimum; (ii) in any other case, 0.3% subject to a Rs 10 lakh maximum.

notes_for_reviewer: Maharashtra Act III of 2021 creates a short-lived era from 9 February 2021 through 19 January 2022: 0.1% up to Rs 5 lakh with a Rs 100 minimum, then 0.3% with a Rs 10 lakh maximum.

source.ref: Maharashtra Act VII of 2022, s.2(3), p.2 (first published 20-Jan-2022)
source.quoted_text: Section 2(3) amends Article 40(b)(ii): the Rs 10 lakh maximum becomes Rs 20 lakh, and an instrument executed in favour of a consortium of banks has a Rs 50 lakh maximum. The Rs 5 lakh threshold, 0.1% lower rate with Rs 100 minimum, and 0.3% upper rate remain.

pending_verification.reason: The Rs 20 lakh or consortium-of-banks Rs 50 lakh ceiling depends on the mortgagee scope. Select consortium of banks or other before computing.

notes_for_reviewer: From 20 January 2022 Maharashtra Act VII retains the two-tier rate and raises the ordinary ceiling to Rs 20 lakh, with a Rs 50 lakh consortium-of-banks ceiling.

source.ref: Maharashtra Stamp Act, 1958, Sch. I Art. 40(b) as it stood before Mah. Act 3 of 2021
source.quoted_text: Sch I Art. 40(b) PRIOR to Mah. Act 3 of 2021 (IGR footnote 6, verbatim): '(b) When possession is not given or agreed to be given as aforesaid — 0.5 percent of the amount secured by such deed, subject to the minimum of one hundred rupee and maximum of ten lakh rupees.' Substituted w.e.f. 9-2-2021 by the current 0.3% / Rs 20 lakh structure.
